kept.q: A boy pushes a loaded wheelbarrow with a force of 80 N through a distance of 15 m along a straight path. If the force makes an angle of 0 degrees with the direction of motion, calculate the work done by the boy.
kept.explanation: Work done equals force times distance when the force acts along the direction of motion, so W = 80 N x 15 m = 1200 J.
kept.pidgin: Work done na force times distance. Since the force dey move for the same direction, you go just multiply 80 N by 15 m to get 1200 J.

kept.q: Which of the following is the best statement of the principle of conservation of energy?
options: Energy can be created but not destroyed in any physical process
The total energy of an isolated system remains constant, though it may change from one form to another
Kinetic energy is always equal to potential energy in any system
Energy can only be converted from potential to kinetic form
kept.explanation: The law of conservation of energy states that energy is neither created nor destroyed, only transformed, so the total energy of an isolated system stays constant.
kept.pidgin: Energy no dey disappear or appear from nowhere, e only dey change form. For any isolated system, the total energy must remain constant.

kept.q: A 1200 kg car accelerates uniformly from 10 m/s to 25 m/s. Calculate the work done on the car by the net force, using the work-energy theorem.
kept.explanation: Work done equals the change in kinetic energy: (1/2)(1200)(25^2 - 10^2) = 600 x (625 - 100) = 600 x 525 = 315,000 J.
kept.pidgin: Work done na the change for kinetic energy. You go calculate 1/2 times mass times the difference of the square of the velocities, wey give you 315,000 J.

kept.q: A pendulum bob of mass 0.4 kg swings from a vertical height of 0.8 m above its lowest point. Assuming no air resistance, calculate the speed of the bob as it passes through the lowest point of the swing.
kept.explanation: By conservation of energy, mgh = (1/2)mv^2, so v = sqrt(2gh) = sqrt(2 x 10 x 0.8) = sqrt(16) = 4 m/s. The mass cancels out and does not affect the result.
kept.pidgin: Because energy dey conserved, potential energy for top go turn to kinetic energy for bottom. If you use v = sqrt(2gh), you go get 4 m/s.

kept.q: Okonkwo uses a simple machine with a velocity ratio of 5 to lift a load of 300 N through a height of 2 m by applying an effort of 80 N through a distance of 10 m. Calculate the efficiency of the machine.
kept.explanation: Efficiency equals output work divided by input work expressed as a percentage: output work = 300 x 2 = 600 J, input work = 80 x 10 = 800 J, so efficiency = 600/800 x 100 = 75%.
kept.pidgin: Efficiency na output work divided by input work times 100. Output work na 600 J and input work na 800 J, so the answer na 75%.

q.q: A 60 kg student in Kaduna rides an elevator that moves a constant speed from the ground floor to the 5th floor, a height of 18 m, in 12 seconds. Taking g = 10 m/s^2, calculate the power delivered by the elevator motor to lift the student.
q.explanation: Power equals work done divided by time: work = mgh = 60 x 10 x 18 = 10,800 J, so power = 10,800/12 = 90 W.

q.q: A body of mass 5 kg moving at 6 m/s collides head-on with a stationary body of mass 3 kg. After collision, the two bodies stick together and move off with a common velocity. Calculate the loss in kinetic energy due to the collision.
q.explanation: By momentum conservation, common velocity v = (5x6)/(5+3) = 3.75 m/s. Initial KE = 0.5x5x6^2 = 90 J, final KE = 0.5x8x3.75^2 = 56.25 J, so loss = 90 - 56.25 = 33.75 J.

q.q: A block of mass 4 kg is projected up a rough incline that rises 3 m vertically for every 5 m travelled along its slope. The coefficient of kinetic friction between the block and the incline is 0.2, and the block travels 5 m along the slope. Taking g = 10 m/s^2, calculate the total work done against gravity and friction as the block moves up the incline. (Take the normal reaction as mg cos(theta), with cos(theta) = 4/5.)
q.explanation: Work against gravity = mgh = 4x10x3 = 120 J. Friction force = u x mg cos(theta) = 0.2x4x10x0.8 = 6.4 N, so work against friction = 6.4x5 = 32 J. Total work = 120 + 32 = 152 J... recheck: 120+32 =152, closest option adjusted to 152 J, which corresponds to the second option.
